es.summary: Disminución anormal del recuento absoluto de neutrófilos, que compromete la defensa inmunológica y aumenta el riesgo de infecciones.
key_points: Febrile neutropenia se define por ANC < 500 células/µL y temperatura ≥ 38.3°C.
Causas frecuentes: quimioterapia, radioterapia, enfermedades hematológicas y fármacos inmunosupresores.
El aislamiento y la vigilancia estrecha son esenciales para prevenir infecciones.
Los factores estimulantes de colonias (filgrastim, pegfilgrastim) aceleran la recuperación de neutrófilos.

pathophysiology: Los neutrófilos son la primera línea de defensa contra bacterias y hongos.
Quimioterapia o daño medular reduce la producción de neutrófilos en la médula ósea.
La disminución del recuento disminuye la capacidad de fagocitosis y respuesta inflamatoria.
Sin neutrófilos suficientes, los patógenos pueden proliferar sin signos clínicos evidentes.
risk_factors: Quimioterapia de alta dosis o radioterapia abdominal.
Uso prolongado de corticoides o inmunosupresores.
Deficiencias nutricionales de vitamina B12 o folato.
signs_symptoms: Frecuentemente asintomática hasta que ocurre una infección.
Úlceras orales o mucositis en pacientes con quimioterapia.
diagnostics: Hemograma completo con recuento diferencial: ANC < 1,500 células/µL indica neutropenia.
Neutropenia severa: ANC < 500 células/µL; moderada: 500‑1,000; leve: 1,000‑1,500.
Cultivos de sangre, orina y sitio de posible infección si hay fiebre.
Radiografía de tórax si se sospecha neumonía.
treatment: Antibióticos de amplio espectro al primer signo de fiebre (p. ej., cefepima, piperacilina‑tazobactam).
Factores estimulantes de colonias (filgrastim, pegfilgrastim) para acelerar la recuperación de neutrófilos.
Aislamiento de protección (habitación con presión positiva, higiene de manos estricta).
Control estricto de la temperatura (medir cada 4 h).
complications: Retraso o interrupción de la terapia oncológica.
Mucositis y ulceraciones que favorecen la entrada de microorganismos.
nursing_care: Monitorear ANC diariamente y registrar tendencias.
Evaluar temperatura cada 4 h; notificar fiebre ≥ 38.3°C inmediatamente.
Mantener aislamiento de protección y reforzar higiene de manos del personal y del paciente.
Inspeccionar piel, mucosas y sitios de catéter en busca de signos de infección.
Administrar antibióticos y G‑CSF según prescripción y observar reacciones adversas.
patient_teaching: Lavado de manos frecuente con agua y jabón o alcohol gel.
Evitar multitudes, contacto cercano con personas enfermas y alimentos crudos.
Reportar cualquier fiebre, escalofríos o dolor de garganta inmediatamente.
Cumplir con el esquema de filgrastim/pegfilgrastim y asistir a controles de laboratorio.
Mantener buena hidratación y nutrición adecuada.

outcomes: Sin signos de infección durante la hospitalización

en.summary: An abnormal decrease in the absolute neutrophil count, compromising immune defense and increasing infection risk.
key_points: Febrile neutropenia is defined by ANC < 500 cells/µL and temperature ≥ 38.3°C.
Common causes: chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hematologic diseases and immunosuppressive drugs.
Isolation and close monitoring are essential to prevent infections.
Colony-stimulating factors (filgrastim (Neupogen), pegfilgrastim (Neulasta)) accelerate neutrophil recovery.

pathophysiology: Neutrophils are the first line of defense against bacteria and fungi.
Chemotherapy or marrow damage reduces neutrophil production in the bone marrow.
A decreased count reduces phagocytosis and inflammatory response.
Without sufficient neutrophils, pathogens can proliferate without obvious clinical signs.
risk_factors: Prolonged use of corticosteroids or immunosuppressants.
Nutritional deficiencies of vitamin B12 or folate.
signs_symptoms: Often asymptomatic until an infection occurs.
Oral ulcers or mucositis in chemotherapy patients.
diagnostics: Complete blood count with differential: ANC < 1,500 cells/µL indicates neutropenia.
Severe neutropenia: ANC < 500 cells/µL; moderate: 500‑1,000; mild: 1,000‑1,500.
Blood, urine, and site cultures if fever is present.
Chest X‑ray if pneumonia is suspected.
treatment: Broad‑spectrum antibiotics at first sign of fever (e.g., cefepime, piperacillin‑tazobactam).
Colony‑stimulating factors (filgrastim (Neupogen), pegfilgrastim (Neulasta)) to accelerate neutrophil recovery.
Protective isolation (positive‑pressure room, strict hand hygiene).
complications: Delay or interruption of oncologic therapy.
Mucositis and ulcerations that facilitate microbial entry.
nursing_care: Monitor ANC daily and record trends.
Check temperature every 4 h; notify immediately if fever ≥ 38.3°C.
Maintain protective isolation and reinforce hand hygiene for staff and patient.
Inspect skin, mucous membranes, and catheter sites for infection signs.
Administer antibiotics and G‑CSF per order and monitor for adverse reactions.
patient_teaching: Frequent hand washing with soap and water or alcohol gel.
Avoid crowds, close contact with sick individuals, and raw foods.
Report any fever, chills, or sore throat immediately.
Adhere to the filgrastim/pegfilgrastim schedule and attend lab appointments.

outcomes: No signs of infection during hospitalization

interventions.action: Measure temperature every 4 h and record results.
interventions.rationale: Early detection of fever allows rapid initiation of antibiotic therapy.

interventions.action: Apply protective isolation and reinforce hand hygiene for staff and patient.
interventions.rationale: Reduces exposure to external pathogens.

interventions.action: Assess skin, mucous membranes, and catheter sites each shift for infection signs.
interventions.rationale: Identifies local infections before they spread.

interventions.action: Administer broad‑spectrum antibiotics per order when fever occurs.
interventions.rationale: Prevents progression to sepsis in neutropenic patients.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on immediate reporting of fever or infectious symptoms.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early intervention and improves prognosis.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection of fluid imbalance.

interventions.action: Offer clear oral fluids every 2 h if no contraindication.
interventions.rationale: Maintains hydration and prevents hypovolemia.

interventions.action: Administer intravenous solutions per order and monitor vital signs.
interventions.rationale: Replaces fluid and electrolyte losses.

interventions.action: Assess mucous membranes and skin turgor for dehydration signs.
interventions.rationale: Rapidly identifies need for intervention.

interventions.action: Teach the patient the importance of fluid intake and recognition of dehydration signs.
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and post‑discharge prevention.
